lines.en: Andre, did you see that? We were about to leave for the mountains when the hail started, and the whole sky turned black.
lines.pt: Andre, você viu aquilo? Estávamos prestes a sair para as montanhas quando o granizo começou, e o céu inteiro ficou preto.

lines.en: I watched it from the kitchen! The lights flickered, and I was about to call you when the power came back on.
lines.pt: Eu vi da cozinha! As luzes piscaram, e eu estava prestes a ligar para você quando a energia voltou.

lines.en: It was so loud. A piece of hail hit the windshield, and I honestly thought the glass was going to shatter.
lines.pt: Foi tão alto. Uma pedra de granizo bateu no para-brisa, e eu achei mesmo que o vidro ia estilhaçar.

lines.en: Is it damaged? My neighbor's car got hit, and now he needs a whole new windshield.
lines.pt: Ficou danificado? O carro do meu vizinho foi atingido, e agora ele precisa de um para-brisa inteiro novo.

lines.en: Only a small crack, luckily. We waited inside until it passed, and my wife said it was safer to cancel the trip.
lines.pt: Só uma rachadura pequena, por sorte. Esperamos lá dentro até passar, e minha esposa disse que era mais seguro cancelar a viagem.

lines.en: Sensible. When I was a kid, a storm like that ruined our camping trip too. My dad was about to pitch the tent when it started.
lines.pt: Sensato. Quando eu era criança, uma tempestade assim também estragou nosso acampamento. Meu pai estava prestes a montar a barraca quando começou.

lines.en: I hate it when a trip gets canceled at the last minute. After weeks of planning, it feels like such a waste.
lines.pt: Odeio quando uma viagem é cancelada na última hora. Depois de semanas de planejamento, parece um grande desperdício.

lines.en: At first, yes. But we played cards by the fire all night, and honestly, it was better than any camping trip I remember.
lines.pt: No começo, sim. Mas jogamos cartas perto da lareira a noite toda e, sinceramente, foi melhor que qualquer acampamento de que me lembro.

lines.en: That's the good thing about storms. They force everybody to stop. We even started arguing about the route, but then we just laughed.
lines.pt: Essa é a graça das tempestades. Elas obrigam todo mundo a parar. Chegamos a discutir sobre a rota, mas aí só rimos.

lines.en: Exactly. So, do you still want to go this weekend, if the forecast improves? I can check the cabin prices tonight.
lines.pt: Exato. Então, você ainda quer ir neste fim de semana, se a previsão melhorar? Posso ver os preços da cabana hoje à noite.

lines.en: Definitely. Let me look at the forecast after dinner, and if it's clear, I'll book a cabin near the lake.
lines.pt: Com certeza. Deixe-me ver a previsão depois do jantar, e se estiver limpo, reservo uma cabana perto do lago.

facts.label: We were about to leave when it started
facts.sub: prestes a + infinitivo · when marca a interrupção

facts.label: was about to
facts.sub: Was/were about to + verbo mostra o instante logo antes de algo: I was about to phone you. Sempre use o infinitivo sem outras formas, como leave, call, park.

facts.label: …when it started
facts.sub: Com when, a frase mostra o que interrompeu: We were about to leave when the hail started. O evento depois de when fica no passado simples.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: I was about to leave means I was almost leaving.
We say I was about to leaving.
items.why: Use the infinitive: about to leave.

items.s: When introduces the event that interrupted.

extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: I was about to leave means I was almost leaving. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
We say I was about to leaving. → Falso (Use the infinitive: about to leave.)
When introduces the event that interrupted. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)

pages.title: We were about to leave when it started · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a hot afternoon in Denver. Tess packs a bag by the front door. Theo waits in the kitchen with a book. The mountains look clear in the distance. Then the sky starts to change. A cold wind blows.

“Theo, we were about to leave for the mountains when the hail started, and suddenly the whole sky turned black.” says Tess. “I saw it from the kitchen. I was about to phone you when the lights went out for a moment.” says Theo. “I was about to lock the front door when a piece of hail hit the windscreen. It was loud!” says Tess.
